Kuwait Petroleum Corp Insolvency Sends Shockwaves Through National Energy Sector

KUWAIT CITY—Kuwait Petroleum Corp, the country's flagship oil and gas producer, has entered insolvency proceedings, sending ripples of uncertainty through Kuwait’s vital energy sector. The insolvency, announced late Monday evening, has already disrupted company operations, with ongoing projects suspended and supply contracts thrown into doubt.

As of Tuesday morning, Kuwait Petroleum Corp’s refineries in Shuaiba and Mina Abdullah had reduced output to minimum levels, according to sources familiar with the matter. Company officials cited “unprecedented financial distress” as the reason for the drastic slowdown. “We are making every effort to stabilize operations while complying with legal requirements,” said acting CEO Nasser Al-Haroun in a statement. “Our priority is to ensure the safety of our staff and to protect what assets we can during this difficult time.”

Industry analysts estimate that the company’s current production has fallen by at least 40%, with further declines expected as the insolvency process continues. The National Oil Workers Union expressed deep concern for the 13,000 employees whose jobs now hang in the balance. “Families are anxious and demand transparency about their future,” said union leader Faisal Al-Rashidi. “We urge the government to step in and safeguard livelihoods.”

The Kuwait Oil & Gas Association warned that the insolvency could have broader implications for the country’s export commitments and downstream industries. “Kuwait Petroleum Corp is central to both domestic supply and international contracts,” said association chair Amal Al-Sabah. “The disruption is already being felt by key partners and local businesses that depend on steady fuel deliveries.”

Court-appointed administrators from Al-Khalij Restructuring LLP have begun reviewing the company’s assets and obligations. For now, uncertainty looms as stakeholders await further updates while Kuwait Petroleum Corp’s insolvency proceedings unfold.
